summary: Flaky: TestOnsaleLoadProof fails on a single 5xx in 250 requests (observed during TKT-134)
description:
Observed during TKT-134's gate runs, on a tree whose only change was a test file in a different Go module (`services/inventory/internal/store`), so it cannot have been caused by that work.

```
onsale_load_test.go:283: stage sustained  offered=250 started=250 dropped=0 ok=249 rejected=0
                         client-err=0 server-err=1 inflight max/peak=64/1
                         hold p50/p95/p99=2.7/3.9/4.5ms lifecycle p50/p95/p99=5.8/8.1/10.4ms
                         lag p99=2.2ms achieved=25.0 ok/s
onsale_load_test.go:385: 1 attempts hit server-side errors before the fill (5xx/unexpected status/malformed body)
--- FAIL: TestOnsaleLoadProof (11.81s)
```

Passed on an immediate re-run of the identical tree (`EXIT=0`, `PASS: TestOnsaleLoadProof (12.80s)`).

**The diagnostic already exists — corrected 2026-08-26.** This ticket originally asked, as its first
item, for the test to be made capable of saying *what* the 5xx was. It already is, and was when the
ticket was filed. Every `KindServerError` return carries a `Note` with the status code and the first
200 bytes of the body (`smoke/onsale_load_test.go:123,141,149,161,165,172`), the runner retains the
first three (`smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:134-141`), and `logStage` prints them as
`stage <name> error sample: …` **immediately before** the stats line (`onsale_load_test.go:278-281`).
All of it shipped in TKT-92 (`9254e057`).

The capture above starts at the stats line, so the sample line — if one was emitted — sits just above
what was pasted. **The first action is therefore retrieval, not code.**

**What to establish:**
- [ ] Recover the error sample for this failure: find the full TKT-134 gate-run log and read the
      lines immediately preceding `onsale_load_test.go:283`. If the log is gone, reproduce with
      `make onsale-load-full` (or a repeated gate run) and capture the sample.
- [ ] With the response in hand: whether a lone server error in 250 attempts should fail the proof at
      all. TKT-92/93 set this harness's error taxonomy; a zero-tolerance threshold on a load test
      that shares a machine with the rest of the gate may be the wrong bar — or may be exactly right,
      in which case the 5xx is a real defect and this is not a flake ticket.
- [ ] Same discipline as TKT-132/134: no `-count=N`. Either identify the failing response, or force
      the condition deterministically.

**The trap, restated because it decides the ticket.** The tempting fix — tolerate 1 error in 250 — is
the bounded-replacement shape AGENTS.md warns about: a proof that tolerates an *unexplained* 5xx has
quietly lowered the NFR TKT-82 established. Tolerate only with the response identified and the
rationale written down.

**Where this runs.** The **gate** profile of `TestOnsaleLoadProof` runs inside `make check` (`check`
depends on `smoke`); only the **full** NFR profile is the on-demand `onsale-load-full` target
(`Makefile:175-182`). So the "shares a loaded machine with the rest of the gate" framing is accurate.

**Note the pattern.** This was the third flake in this area (TKT-132 recovery sweep, TKT-134 lazy
release, this). All three are timing-sensitive assertions over a shared, loaded stack.
**TKT-132, TKT-134, TKT-198, TKT-213 and TKT-218 are now all Done — this is the last one open.**
Worth asking once whether the gate's smoke stage needs isolation guarantees it does not currently
have, rather than fixing them one at a time.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness — CONCERNS (shaped 2026-08-08)

Filed unshaped; Gate 1 was hard-blocking it. Shaped now.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | OK | No gate failure on one transient 5xx; still catches a real regression |
| Scope | OK | The load proof's error accounting only |
| Uncertainties | **WARN** | The 5xx is unexplained — it may be the finding, not the noise |
| Dependencies | OK | None |
| Approach | **WARN** | Diagnose before tolerating |
| AC verifiable | OK | Must prove the proof can still fail |
| Context-mémo | OK | Re-resolved today |

**Concern:** the tempting fix — allow 1 error in 250 — is exactly the move `AGENTS.md` warns about
with bounded replacements: *a bounded or optimized replacement is a new implementation, so ask what
the version it replaced would have caught*. A proof that tolerates an unexplained 5xx has quietly
lowered the NFR TKT-82 established. Diagnose first; tolerate only with a stated rationale.

**Lowest urgency of the three test-integrity tickets** (TKT-198 red now, TKT-218 fails open, this one
fails closed and rarely) — but it is also the cheapest to make diagnosable, which is the first slice.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ⚠️ MATERIAL CORRECTION — the first acceptance criterion is already satisfied, and was when the ticket was filed

Backlog review 2026-08-26 at HEAD `1aaee7cd`. **Still hold at Gate 1, but for a different reason than the ticket gives.**

**AC #1 is false.** The ticket says the assertion *"reports a count, not the response — so the test proves 'something 5xx'd' and cannot say what, which is the first thing to fix regardless of the outcome"*, and the earlier readiness comment calls that the cheapest first slice. The capability already exists and predates the ticket:

- Every `KindServerError` path sets a diagnostic `Note` with status code + 200 chars of body — six sites at `smoke/onsale_load_test.go:123,141,149,161,165,172`.
- The runner retains the first three: `smoke/internal/loadtest/loadtest.go:137-141` (`ErrorNotes`).
- `logStage` prints them immediately before the stats line: `smoke/onsale_load_test.go:280-281`.

All shipped in **TKT-92 (`9254e057`)**. Confirmed against the contemporaneous tree — `git show c46440cb:smoke/onsale_load_test.go` (last commit before 2026-07-31) already has the `ErrorNotes` loop and all six `Note` sites. So the failure pasted in the ticket **should have been preceded by a `stage sustained error sample: …` line**; either the paste was trimmed or it was not read.

**What is genuinely intact.** Zero tolerance is still in force (`onsale_load_test.go:409-411` pre-fill, `:451-453` post-reject, both `t.Fatalf` on `ServerErrors != 0`), and the TKT-92/93 taxonomy is unchanged (`loadtest.go:132-141`).

**One more framing correction.** The earlier comment ranks this *"lowest urgency of the three test-integrity tickets — TKT-198 red now, TKT-218 fails open"*. TKT-132, TKT-134, TKT-198, TKT-213 and TKT-218 are **all Done**. This is the last one standing. It is also not in `make check` — it is the on-demand `onsale-load-full` target (`Makefile:175-178`), so the "shares a machine with the rest of the gate" argument needs re-checking against how it is actually invoked.

**The next action is a retrieval, not a ticket.** Strike AC #1, then recover the full TKT-134 gate-run log with its `error sample` line — or re-run `make onsale-load-full` and capture one. Only then is the remaining question (is one 5xx in 250 a defect or acceptable noise?) answerable, and the AGENTS.md trap the earlier comment names is exactly right: do not tolerate an unexplained 5xx, because a proof that does has quietly lowered TKT-82's NFR.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Description corrected — the false first AC is struck

Re-verified at HEAD `1aaee7cd` before editing, not inherited from the review pass that found it.

**Struck:** *"The assertion reports a count, not the response — so the test proves 'something 5xx'd'
and cannot say what, which is the first thing to fix regardless of the outcome."* The capability
shipped in TKT-92 (`9254e057`) and predates this ticket: six `Note` sites
(`onsale_load_test.go:123,141,149,161,165,172`), retention at `loadtest.go:134-141`, printed at
`onsale_load_test.go:278-281` **above** the stats line. The pasted capture begins at the stats line,
which is why no sample appears in it.

**Replaced with** a retrieval step, which is what the ticket actually needs first.

**One correction to the previous review comment on this ticket, which was wrong.** It said the test
is "not in `make check` — it's the on-demand `onsale-load-full` target". Only the *full* profile is
on-demand. `check` depends on `smoke` (`Makefile:17`), and `TestOnsaleLoadProof` runs its **gate**
profile there (`onsale_load_test.go:366-372`). The ticket's "shares a machine with the rest of the
gate" reasoning stands, and the description now says so explicitly.

**Also updated:** the sibling-flake note. All four siblings are Done; this is the last one open.

Still held at Gate 1 — the remaining question (is one 5xx in 250 a defect or noise?) is unanswerable
until the response is identified.

objective.note: TestOnsaleLoadProof does not fail the gate for a single transient 5xx in 250 requests, without becoming unable to detect a real server-error regression.

scope.note: services/.../onsale_load_test.go and its error accounting. Not the on-sale NFR targets themselves (TKT-82).

uncertainties.note: OPEN: what produced the single 5xx? Until that is known, any tolerance is a guess. A load proof that tolerates errors it cannot explain is weaker than one that fails - the 5xx may be the finding.

approach.note: OPEN. Explain the 5xx first (capture the response body/status on failure if it is not already captured); only then decide whether a bounded tolerance is honest or whether the error is a real defect to fix.

first_slice.note: Make the failure diagnosable: record what the failing request actually returned, so the next occurrence answers the question instead of re-raising it.

success.note: Either the 5xx is explained and fixed, or a tolerance is introduced WITH its rationale and a test proving the proof still fails on a sustained error rate.
